corrections.text: The article attributes the detail that Adam Raine's interactions with ChatGPT "allegedly contributed to isolating him from his family and friends" to the CalMatters article at economy/technology/2026/09/california-enacts-laws-restricting-chatbots-protecting-kids-online/. That article does not contain this detail; it only reports that Raine "died by suicide in 2025 after receiving tips from ChatGPT." The isolation detail is reported by CalMatters' separate mental-health article (health/mental-health/2026/09/newsom-online-child-protections/), which states he "died by suicide last year after coaching by ChatGPT isolated him from his family and friends." The fact is accurate; it was cited to the wrong one of the article's two CalMatters sources.
